summary: z/OS adds a third file mode, EBCDIC text, which Ansible does not handle, so users must convert files themselves. File tags mark files as binary, UTF-8 or EBCDIC, but Ansible modules ignore tags and send untagged UTF-8, so tagging needs an extra command task.
questions: Does Ansible handle EBCDIC files on z/OS?
Will Ansible preserve or read the file tag on a z/OS file?
How are files Ansible sends to z/OS encoded?
How do I tag a file on z/OS from a playbook?

answer_card.title: EBCDIC encoding and file tags on z/OS
answer_card.answer_md:
Besides binary and UTF-8 text, z/OS has a third mode: **EBCDIC-encoded text**. Ansible handles binary and UTF-8 but not EBCDIC, so you need extra tasks to convert files to and from their original encodings.

z/OS UNIX uses **file tags** (part of Enhanced ASCII) to record whether a file is binary, UTF-8 text or EBCDIC text. Untagged files are interpreted by the reading program (for example IBM Open Enterprise SDK for Python defaults to UTF-8).

Ansible modules don't read or recognize tags. Data Ansible sends is UTF-8 and untagged by default, so tag files yourself with a command task (for example `chtag`).
